messages:
ashwin: Quick sync — silkroad model intake. We need to close owners + licensing + perf profile before catalog rollout. TL;DR: who's owning platform changes, is the license deploy-safe, and do we have a perf baseline? :wave:

maria_legal: I looked at the model repo license. It's a mixed bundle: tokenizer under Apache-2.0, model weights under CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. That NC part blocks commercial hosted usage unless we negotiate. Need legal review + opt-in from upstream or a different variant. :thinking_face:

ben_platform: @ashwin noted — from infra side, memory/shape looks OK but we need to validate quantized checkpoint. If we can't host the canonical weights due to license, we should confirm there's a permissive mirror or quantized fork. Planning a quick compatibility pass on a g4dn instance. ETA ~ tomorrow. :eyes:

leah_research: Ran a small micro-benchmark on the provided weights (local). Results: 
```
model: silkroad-7b-fp16
seq=512, batch=1
p95 latency: 210ms
tokens/sec (generation): ~85
memory peak (gpu): 11.3GB
```
Quantized to int8-lite gave ~1.8x speedup but +2-3% perplexity bump on our eval set. Full eval report with eval set link will follow. Not blocking but flagging quality delta.

ashwin: Thanks @leah_research. Can you put the eval link in this thread when ready? Also, @maria_legal any chance to get an exception request template? If upstream can't relicense we need to know what write-up to ask for.

maria_legal: I'll draft an exception request template by EOD. If they don't grant reuse for commercial, we can still list the model in catalog with a "read-only / research" tag but must hide it from hosted API routes. That requires a routing rule change from platform.

ben_platform: Good call. If it's "research-only" we'll need a model-visibility flag and a policy to prevent accidental routing. I can add a feature flag and an allowlist mapping. Putting a low-risk PR in staging today: `feat: model-visibility-guard`. Will link CI.

deploy-bot: CI: model-ingest-lint — failed (checksum mismatch). See: https://ci.redwood/proj/ingest/4321/logs.

tim_ops: Re: canary plan — if legal/visibility is sorted, proposed canary: 1% traffic for 2 hours, 5% for 4 hours, evaluate latency/error/quality metrics. Rollback if error rate >1% or median latency increases >25%. Need owners to sign off on metrics and a rollback owner.

ashwin: I'll own rollout coordination and rollback. @leah_research will own quality signals (eval set + manual review), @ben_platform owns deploy controls, @tim_ops owns runbook + monitoring thresholds, @maria_legal owns licensing follow-up.

leah_research: Uploaded eval artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/silkroad/bench/2026-03-17 (includes per-prompt diffs). Early note: prompt-set A had 3 prompts with hallucination regressions vs our baseline — I opened an issue with examples.

ben_platform: Linking staging PR: https://git.redwood/infra/feat-model-visibility/pull/98. CI now fixed local env; will rerun ingest after ingest-lint fix.

maria_legal: Exception template posted: https://confluence.redwood/legal/model-exception-template. If the upstream says no, we can proceed as research-only and document limitations.

ashwin: Blocker list for next 24h: (1) legal template finalized (maria) (2) ingest-lint fixed + checksum pass (ben) (3) full eval + diffs (leah) (4) feature-flag PR merged to staging (ben) (5) canary schedule finalized (tim). If any of you can't hit these, call it out now. :pray:

ben_platform: On it — expect ingest-lint fix within 3hrs.

leah_research: Full eval upload ETA 6hrs. Adding a short quality checklist for canary reviewers.

tim_ops: I'll draft canary playbook and post it here in ~2hrs.

maria_legal: Template done. Will start outreach if you want me to.

ashwin: Great — thanks all. If no blockers by EOD, I'll schedule a 1% canary tomorrow morning and post a final rollout note. :thumbsup:
